verdict.rationale: Crossmint requires explicit user authorization before agents can spend. Card spending runs through an order intent the user authorizes, with passkey or card-network verification, a fixed amount, expiry and a locked merchant. Wallet spending uses a signer key bound to a permission set the user signs off on (spend cap, counterparties, time window), enforced onchain and revocable. Missing for 10: wallet delegation explicitly runs with "no user prompt per action", so per-purchase consent is limited to the card and order-intent flow; there is no documented threshold-based escalation for higher-risk spends; and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.
